scope: what the replay does when the event-lineage graph of a date is genuinely ambiguous, and therefore whether the ambiguous-lineage refusal can stop an automated run

authorization.options_presented: docs/implementation/PHASE_4B_2026-09-09.md §16.4, three deterministic rules with the measured cost of each
authorization.standing_requirement: nothing that requires human review may remain in the final production system
authorization.why_the_owner: the rule states what the system means by 'this detection continues that event'. That is scientific. The executing agent measured the consequence, retracted its own earlier recommendation, and escalated rather than choosing.

decided.rule_in_words: a detection whose lineage is genuinely ambiguous is recorded as a NEW event, and the ambiguity is recorded with it. The system never assigns an ancestry it cannot determine.
decided.applies_to: the Phase 4 replay only; the blue runtime keeps raising

what_counts_as_ambiguous.condition: a detection that overlaps more than one eligible event, where at least one of those events also overlaps more than one detection — the many-to-many split/merge component the accepted Package 2A.1 contract fails closed on
what_counts_as_ambiguous.what_is_dropped: only the links of the detections matching that condition. Their unambiguous neighbours inside the same component keep their lineage: a detection with exactly one parent continues that parent, as it does today.
what_counts_as_ambiguous.why_not_the_whole_component: the single-parent detections in a tangle are not ambiguous — they clearly continue one event. Discarding their lineage too would lose real information for no gain.
what_counts_as_ambiguous.sufficiency_verified: dropping exactly those links silences BOTH branches of the guard. Brute-forced over all 682 bipartite graphs up to 3 detections by 3 events: the original guard raises if and only if that set is non-empty, and links are only ever removed, so no new violation can appear. The guard is re-checked after the drop rather than assumed silent.

measured_stakes.measured_on: 2026-09-16, with scripts/measure_lineage_ambiguity.py against the replay's own state and composites
measured_stakes.component_shapes: almost all 2 detections x 2 events or 3 x 2; largest observed 8 x 4
measured_stakes.reading: the whole date is discarded because of 0.13% to 0.39% of it. The year fell from 90 dates to 3 for that reason.

rejected.largest_overlap_wins: asserts an ancestry that, in a 2x2 tangle, is a near-tie by construction, so the assignment has no physical basis. It is also LESS faithful than the behaviour beside it: for a detection with several parents and no tangle, update_tracks already mints a merge child recording ALL parents, and this rule would pick one and discard the rest. The executing agent recommended this first, without having read that neighbouring path, and retracted it.
rejected.whole_component_becomes_a_merge: preserves the ancestry and is the natural extension of the existing merge, but on the measured 8 x 4 component it fuses eight detections over four events into one lineage, after which area per event means something different.

why_c_and_not_the_other_two.why_this_one: with 0.1-0.4% at stake the value of getting the ancestry right is small and the cost of asserting a wrong one is permanent, because it reaches the publication. This is the only one of the three that never asserts what is not known, it is the easiest to state in a paper, and it leaves the other ~2000 components of each date identical to today.

what_is_recorded_when_it_fires.per_detection: lineage_ambiguity_resolved, true on the detections that became origin events because their lineage could not be determined
what_is_recorded_when_it_fires.per_date: the count travels in the returned frame's persistence_transition attributes, so the replay driver records it per date without re-deriving it
what_is_recorded_when_it_fires.why_recording_matters: option (c) is defensible in a publication only if the affected detections are enumerable. 'Ambiguous lineage cases were treated as new events' is a claim that needs a number and a list behind it.

does_not_change.blue_default: the parameter defaults to raise, so src/detection/persistence.py and the scheduled pipeline behave exactly as before. Verified equivalent by brute force, not by inspection.
does_not_change.the_guard_itself: AmbiguousLineageError is not removed and still raises in the blue default, and is re-checked after the drop in the replay mode.
does_not_change.the_overlap_rule: min_overlap_frac stays at the owner's 0.55 for the replay and 0.05 for blue.
does_not_change.output_schema_of_blue: the per-detection column is added only when the rule is active, so the blue alert files keep their exact property set.

what_this_does_not_settle.the_production_cutover: the blue runtime still raises. Carrying this rule into the scheduled pipeline is a Phase 6 change with its own review, and the owner's no-human-review requirement applies to it there.
what_this_does_not_settle.persistence_v2_and_v3: each holds its own copy of the guard and its own default. They are imported only by validators today; switching the runtime to v3 would reinstate the refusal.
what_this_does_not_settle.the_other_six_stop_conditions: six further PersistenceTransitionError subclasses still stop the blue workflow. See docs/implementation/PHASE_4B_2026-09-09.md §14.2.
what_this_does_not_settle.whether_continuity_loss_matters_scientif: the rule loses the streak of 9 to 47 detections per date. Phase 5 owns whether that matters for the validated claims, and now has the per-date list.
